newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Banking stands out as Fortis Q1 rises 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Banking stands out as Fortis Q1 rises 30 pct.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis reaped an immediate benefit from its expanded banking operations by delivering a higher than expected increase in first quarter profits on Wednesday.
Fortis, jointly owned by Fortis Amev of the Netherlands and Belgium's Fortis AG , also shed its previous caution by forecasting a 10 to 15 percent lift in full year earnings.
Net profit was 204 million ECUs ($233.4 million) in the first three months of 1997, up 30 percent from 157 million ECUs in the first three months of 1996.
The result was applauded by analysts and shares in the two parent companies jumped to new highs before settling back at lower levels.
Net profits from banking increased by 83 percent in the first quarter of 1997 while those from insurance advanced 13 percent.
Fortis said earnings were boosted by MeesPierson, the investment bank acquired from the Dutch bank ABN AMRO effective January 1 for 2.5 billion guilders, and by a recovery in the United States.
"As expected MeesPierson immediately made a positive contribution," it said.
Fortis said the nature of its banking activities had changed with the purchase of MeesPierson, citing the increased importance of commissions and financial transactions.
The group also said the result from its Dutch VSB Bank unit developed satisfactorily as a result of higher commissions and cost control.

Operating profits in the United States more than trebled as a result of a powerful recovery in life insurance and a better performance from accident and health insurance, partly because of the disposal of a number of loss-making activities.
But operating profits from the insurance sector in Belgium fell, due in part to frost-damage claims and lower life insurance results from ASLK-CGER Insurance.
Currencies also had a negative impact on results.
Fortis said that for the whole of 1997 it expected group net profits and earnings per share of its two parent companies to rise by 10 to 15 percent.
When it announced 1996 results in March, Fortis forecast higher full year profits but declined to be more specific.

"On the basis of the results for the first quarter, Fortis is filling out its previous forecast, although it does not expect the high percentage in the first quarter of 1997 to be achieved for the year as a whole," the group said.
Analysts had been expecting the group's first-quarter earnings to rise an average of about 18 percent.
"It's substantially better, and my estimate wasn't that pessimistic," ING Barings analyst Daan Worm said.
Fortis Amev shares on the Amsterdam stock exchange jumped to a 1997 high of 84.50 guilders after the result before easing to 82.70 at 1145 GMT, up 1.20 on the day.
In Brussels, Fortis AG shares rose to a year's peak fo 7200 Belgian francs in response to the announcement, but settled back later at 6,980, up 60 francs on the day.
Dennis Ederzeel of Delta Lloyd Bank estimated that MeesPierson contributed about half of the 30 percent increase in net profits.
Rabo Securities analyst Bart van der Feen said VSB was performing better as a result of cost controls after several years of meagre earnings.
"The quality of the results is very good. The stock should be qualified as a strong buy," he said.
